segments.t: On the park bench, a gentle silence settles between Andrea Martel and Colette Brancillon after their painful agreement. Moved by Andrea's unprecedented honesty, Colette shares a tender final kiss that seals their parting with love and respect. Let's listen to their words in French first.
Tu ne dis rien, Colette?
J'écoute ce que tu me dis.
Tu ne m'as pas vraiment répondu.
Regarde-moi dans les yeux, Andréa.
Je te regarde avec tout mon cœur.
Tu n'as jamais été aussi sincère.
Je veux seulement être juste aujourd'hui.
Laisse-moi t'embrasser une dernière fois.
C'est un baiser d'adieu?
C'est un baiser de respect mutuel.
Je n'oublierai jamais nos moments partagés.
Moi non plus, chère Andréa.
Merci pour ta tendresse et ton écoute.
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Tu ne dis rien, Colette?
'You say nothing, Colette?' Andrea wonders about the long silence between them. The negative pronoun 'nothing' means nothing.
J'écoute ce que tu me dis.
'I am listening to what you tell me.' Colette reflects on Andrea's thoughtful words. The verb 'ecoute' comes from 'ecouter', to listen.
Tu ne m'as pas vraiment répondu.
'You did not really answer me.' Andrea notices that Colette has remained quiet. The compound past 'have' comes from 'answered'.
Regarde-moi dans les yeux, Andréa.
'Look at me in the eyes, Andrea.' Colette turns toward her with warm affection. The imperative 'look' combines the verb with an object pronoun.
Je te regarde avec tout mon cœur.
'I look at you with all my heart.' Andrea returns her steady, open gaze. The noun 'heart' designates the heart.
Tu n'as jamais été aussi sincère.
'You have never been so sincere.' Colette appreciates Andrea's absolute emotional truth. The adjective 'sincere' means honest or candid.
Je veux seulement être juste aujourd'hui.
'I only want to be fair today.' Andrea explains her desire for clear honesty. The restrictive adverb 'only' means only.
Laisse-moi t'embrasser une dernière fois.
'Let me kiss you one last time.' Colette leans in softly toward Andrea. The verb 'kiss' means to kiss.
C'est un baiser d'adieu?
'Is this a goodbye kiss?' Andrea whispers softly as their lips touch. The compound noun 'baiser d'adieu' signifies a parting kiss.
C'est un baiser de respect mutuel.
'It is a kiss of mutual respect.' Colette honors everything they shared together. The adjective 'mutual' describes reciprocal feelings.
Je n'oublierai jamais nos moments partagés.
'I will never forget our shared moments.' Notice how 'I' sets up the clause and leads naturally into 'shared'.
Moi non plus, chère Andréa.
'Me neither, dear Andrea.' Colette smiles with peaceful finality. The phrase 'me' means me neither.
Merci pour ta tendresse et ton écoute.

'Thank you for your tenderness and listening.' Andrea expresses her heartfelt gratitude. The noun 'tenderness' translates to tenderness or affection. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

Merci pour ta tendresse et ton écoute.

With a gentle kiss and words of gratitude, Andrea and Colette conclude their love story without bitterness. Ready to build separate lives while raising Flora together, they embrace a brighter future. Now let's listen to the scene one last time.
Prends grand soin de notre fille!
